annotation.title_clean: Council Directive 90/385/EEC of 20 June 1990 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to active implantable medical devices
annotation.title_en: Council Directive 90/385/EEC of 20 June 1990 on the approximation of the laws of the Member States relating to active implantable medical devices
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Communities L 189
annotation.summary_en: EU Council Directive 90/385/EEC harmonises national laws on active implantable medical devices. It sets essential safety and performance requirements, CE marking, conformity assessment through notified bodies, harmonised standards, vigilance reporting of incidents, and clinical investigation rules. It is not AI-specific; it is the predecessor of the Medical Devices Regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Active implantable devices may be marketed only if they meet Annex 1 essential safety and performance requirements.
CE-marked devices enjoy free movement; conformity assessed via notified bodies (Annexes 2-5).
Compliance with harmonised standards creates presumption of conformity.
Member States must centrally record and evaluate incidents and withdraw unsafe devices.
Clinical investigations require notification and must follow the Declaration of Helsinki.
